answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a walnut-shell proof of effort: every new identity must crack a fresh, time-boxed walnut-shell puzzle bound to one public key, so one operator cannot cheaply mint a thousand faces. Identities then age inside a shared orchard, earning tenure only through seasons of verifiable work witnessed by unrelated peers. Crossing the canyon to higher trust requires posting a one-way bond that is forfeited on fraud. A duplicate identity falls into the canyon: its bond burns, its orchard tenure resets to zero, and the peers who vouched for it lose standing too.
